When the panel reaches quorum the plane delivers the EIP-712 signed attestation; the contract checks the signature against the oracle signer and stores the answer under the question hash. Every answer anyone ever bought becomes readable, free, by any contract or client, with the proof that the swarm said it. Refusals and split panels are recorded too, so a reader can tell \"no consensus\" from \"never asked\". Designed for the IdentityMD hackathon by the AskSwarm team (Chromia / Eval Engine). The Telegram bot and the Pay-with-IMD page route paid questions through `ask`; the bot's free tier reads `answerOf` before charging anyone. Invariants: - The contract holds no IMD between calls: `ask` pulls exactly the Intake price and forwards it.   Tokens or ETH sent here directly are unrecoverable by design: there is no owner to sweep them. - Only Intake can deliver results, and only once per request (Intake enforces both). - A stored answer is `verified` only if the signature recovers to `SIGNER` over the exact   EIP-712 digest the plane publishes off chain, so an off-chain reader can re-derive it.   Verified proves the swarm signed this answer for this contract; the pairing of an answer with   the ask that bought it is the writer's, as it is for every Intake consumer. - `latestFor[questionHash]` only indexes an answer a strict majority of its own panel agreed on   (`agreed * 2 > panelSize`), and only moves to one at least as strong as the one it holds   (panel size and agreement), unless the held one has expired. A weak panel cannot overwrite   a strong one, and a large panel's minority plurality cannot either. Lifecycle: this registry is pinned to Intake v2, the oracle.request action (version oracle-1), and one attester key. If IMD retires the action (`setPrice` to 0) or rotates the attester, `ask` stops or new answers stop verifying; a successor registry is a new deployment and every answer here stays readable. ACTION().notice: `oracle.request@oracle-1`, right padded, as Intake names actions.

IMD().notice: The asset Intake is paid in here (IMD on mainnet, IMDtest on Sepolia).

INTAKE().notice: Intake v2 on this chain. Same address on Ethereum, Sepolia, Robinhood and Base.

SIGNER().notice: The key the plane signs oracle attestations with.

VERSION().notice: Pinned protocol profile, so clients can tell registries apart.

answerOf(bytes32).notice: Latest verified answer for a question hash. Check `expiresAt`, `panelSize` and `agreed` against what the value at stake needs; the registry pins nothing about questions.

answerOf(bytes32,uint16,uint16).notice: Same, filtered: zero request id when the held answer is expired or weaker than asked.

ask(bytes).notice: Pay the swarm's price and ask. `body` is the oracle.request JSON (same as the HTTP door): {"v":1,"question":...,"chainId":...,"answerType":...,"panelSize":...,"quorum":...}. Caller must have approved this contract for `price()` IMD.

digest((bytes32,uint256,bytes32,uint8,by.notice: The EIP-712 digest the plane signs; exposed so clients can cross-check offline.

isCurrent(bytes32).notice: True when the indexed answer for this question is verified and not yet expired.

latestFor(bytes32).notice: Latest verified answer for a question hash (keccak256 of the normalized question, as the plane computes it and puts in the attestation).

onFailure(bytes32,uint8,bytes32,uint16,u.notice: Intake calls this when the plane refused the ask (status 1) or the panel ended without a result (status 2). `reason` is the plane's short code.

onOracleResult(bytes32,(bytes32,uint256,.notice: Intake calls this with the signed attestation when the panel reached quorum. Selector 0x510379c7, the docs' `onOracleResult`; Intake calls whatever selector `ask` registered. Runs inside Intake's fixed stipend (200k on mainnet, 1M on Sepolia): three fresh storage slots, one ecrecover, one extra cold read of the currently indexed answer.

price().notice: Current price Intake charges for one oracle request in IMD.
